turns.message:
You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

name: arc-stream-actions
description: Handle Continual-ARC puzzle turns: choose a demo request, grid submission, or finish action and obey the exact response protocol.
---

# Act on Continual-ARC instances

1. Use only the current instance's supplied grid, demonstrations, counters, and feedback; do not inspect workspace files, shell state, or artifacts from other tasks. Treat each instance as independent. Record the marker's exact occupied-cell offsets, output changes, unchanged controls, and dimensions. Follow `arc-divider-recolor` for divider-panel tasks and `arc-rectangle-noise` for rectangular fields/frames.
2. Form a precise candidate rule from the demonstrated changes. For any shape-copy or pattern-match hypothesis, enumerate placements/orientations explicitly and verify the complete condition against every demonstration: whether only occupied cells must match, whether the rest of the bounding box/background must also match, and whether rotations/reflections are allowed. Do not broaden a rule from visual resemblance or color alone. If plausible rules remain, request the demo that best distinguishes them; count each request against the budget and incorporate the returned pair before acting again.
3. Submit only once one rule explains all changed and preserved cells in every demo. Construct and independently check the exact output dimensions and cell values, preserving all unaffected cells. Each turn must contain exactly one action JSON object on the final line; do not add commentary or substitute tool output for the action.
4. After incorrect feedback, reject the tested rule and use the counterexample to revise the condition substantively before another submission. Track request and attempt caps. `finish` is permitted only after the instance is over; continue until solved or the cap ends it.

name: arc-divider-recolor
description: Solve ARC grids split by a solid divider, where demonstrations identify which panel supplies the output and how its cells are mapped.
---

# Infer divider-panel outputs

1. In every demonstration, locate the solid divider and measure the panels. Compare output dimensions and cell patterns against each panel (including rotations/reflections only when evidence supports them); determine whether output copies one panel, transforms it, or compares corresponding cells. Do not assume the lower or first panel is selected from orientation alone.
2. Derive the mapping and any cross-panel rule cell by cell from demonstrations. Test every output cell, including cases where candidate inputs differ; reject any rule that misses even one location. Distinguish the candidate's exact condition (for example, a particular color pairing) from merely being in a panel, and track row/column offsets, crop, orientation, and panel dimensions explicitly. If more than one rule fits or none fits, request another demo rather than guessing.
3. Apply only the fully verified rule to the test. Construct the exact demonstrated output dimensions and cell values; independently check each qualifying and nonqualifying position and the separator exclusion before submitting.
